'''''Setaria parviflora''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known by the common names '''marsh bristlegrass''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SEPA10|taxon=Setaria parviflora|accessdate=11 November 2015}}</ref> '''knotroot bristle-grass''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''bristly foxtail''' and '''yellow bristlegrass'''. It is native to North America, including Mexico and the United States from [[California]] to the East Coast, Central America and the West Indies,<ref name=gm>[http://herbarium.usu.edu/webmanual/info2.asp?name=Setaria_parviflora&type=treatment ''Setaria parviflora''.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101116003458/http://herbarium.usu.edu/webmanual/info2.asp?name=setaria_parviflora&type=treatment |date=2010-11-16 }} Grass Manual Treatment.</ref> and South America.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 21 January 2018}}</ref>

This grass is a perennial with small, knotty [[rhizome]]s. It produces stems 30 centimeters to well over one meter tall. The leaf blades are up to 25 centimeters long and under a centimeter wide.<ref name=gm/> The leaves are whitish-green.<ref name=usda>[https://plants.usda.gov/factsheet/pdf/fs_sepa10.pdf ''Setaria parviflora''.] USDA NRCS Plant Fact Sheet.</ref> The [[inflorescence]] is a compact, spikelike [[panicle]] up to 8 or 10 centimeters long. Surrounding each spikelet are up to 12 yellow or purple bristles.<ref name=gm/> The bristles stay on the stalk after the seeds drop away.<ref name=usda/>

This grass grows in moist habitat.<ref name=gm/> It can grow in salty habitat such as [[salt marsh]]es.<ref name=usda/>
